recommended_approach: Pre-fractured glass pane + Active/Passive Rigid Body World: model the window as irregular shard pieces, make the brick and shards ACTIVE rigid bodies, keep the steel frame/wall/floor PASSIVE, keyframe the brick into impact, and use the rigid body animation behavior plus world cache/settings to bake frames 1-60. For the 'remaining glass stays attached then collapses' beat, use the documented rigid-body constraints/animation workflow as the control layer for delayed release.

key_parameters.rigid_body.Animated: Enable while the brick is keyframed/driven into the hit; docs note animated/keyframed rigid bodies need Animated enabled or physics treats them as static/original-pose objects.
key_parameters.rigid_body.steps_per_second: Increase for small, fast glass fragments to improve stability; Blender docs warn that pushing this beyond ~1000 usually indicates the setup should be fixed rather than brute-forced.

warnings: Blender docs state only mesh objects can participate in rigid body simulation, so all glass pieces must be mesh shards.
Blender rigid body tips warn that a keyframed moving object without Animated enabled can move visually while the solver still treats it as static at its original pose.
Rigid body stability guidance says increasing steps_per_second helps accuracy, but excessive values can reduce stability; needing more than about 1000 suggests solving the setup another way.
Bundled API lookup returned some irrelevant armature API hits, so exact scripting properties/operators should be verified against the Blender 5.0 API when implementing automation.
The alternative-technique search was weaker than the core rigid-body documentation, so the primary rigid-body workflow is much better grounded than non-core backups.
alternative_approaches: Pre-cut shard pieces held together with rigid body constraints, then released at impact for more controllable 'still attached then collapse' behavior.
Hero rigid-body simulation for the visible shards, plus an instanced/Geometry-Nodes micro-shard layer for extra fine glass spray while keeping the sim manageable.
